stem.text: A function f has derivative \( f'(x) = \frac{3\left(x + 5\right)\left(x + 1\right)}{x - 4} \) for all \( x \ne 4 \), where f is not defined at \( x = 4 \). On what open intervals is f increasing? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: f is increasing on the intervals \( (-5, -1) \) and \( (4, \infty) \), because \( f'(x) > 0 \) on each of those intervals.

worked_solution.text: The sign of f' can change only where \( f'(x) = 0 \) at \( x = -5 \) and \( x = -1 \), and f' is undefined at \( x = 4 \), which is not in the domain of f.
worked_solution.rule_named: partition points of the sign chart

worked_solution.text: Testing one point in each piece gives \( f'(x) > 0 \) on the intervals \( (-5, -1) \) and \( (4, \infty) \) and \( f'(x) < 0 \) on the intervals \( (-\infty, -5) \) and \( (-1, 4) \).
So f is increasing on the intervals \( (-5, -1) \) and \( (4, \infty) \), because \( f'(x) > 0 \) on each of those intervals.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction of the function

options.label: f is increasing on the intervals \( (-\infty, -5) \) and \( (-1, 4) \), because \( f'(x) > 0 \) on each of those intervals.
options.derivation: the sign of f' read backwards, so the pieces where f' has the opposite sign are reported
